sections.html:
Maryland deeds are recorded through the Clerk of the Circuit Court, in the land records of the county that holds the property.

Each clerk's office has its own intake routine. Take Harford County: the Land Records Department in Bel Air takes documents three ways: e-recording through Simplifile, mail, or walk-in. Walk-ins can bring no more than five documents or sets at once, and finished papers return by U.S. Mail unless the customer requests something else.

Counter hours matter on closing day. Harford's land records counter is open weekdays from 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, though couriers and title companies must arrive by 4:00 PM. Find out from the title company when the deed will really arrive. A late submission can push back the day you get paid.

  • Use the land records of the county where the house stands.
  • Some counties divide the job. In Baltimore County, deeds pass through the Transfer and Recordation Section first and the Circuit Court finalizes them after.
  • Electronic recording through a vendor like Simplifile is another route. The clerk can explain how to set up an account.

sections.h2: Requirements before the clerk accepts a deed
sections.html:
Three things get a deed accepted: a complete intake sheet, proof that taxes are current, and the right fees and taxes. Miss one and the clerk sends the instrument back.

The core rules sit in Real Property Article 3-104. The intake sheet must list the property identifier, parties, instrument type, consideration, recording charges and taxes, claimed exemptions and the tax bill mailing address. A deed also needs a certification that a Maryland attorney, or a party named in the deed, prepared it. The collector must endorse the deed to show that current taxes and charges are paid.

In Baltimore County, a deed that changes ownership and arrives without a lien certificate won't be processed. Deeds for agricultural use and partial transfers first need sign-off from the state assessments department at its Towson office.

Three questions to the title company before closing head off most delays.

  • Has the lien certificate been ordered, and does it reveal unpaid county or municipal charges?
  • Who drafted the deed, and has the preparer certification been signed?
  • If an exemption is claimed, does the intake sheet carry the correct code?

sections.h2: What it costs to record a deed
sections.html:
Expect a per-document recording fee and a flat surcharge, with taxes billed on top of both. The clerk's fee depends mainly on page count and on whether the property is a principal residence. Cecil and Harford counties use the same structure.

ChargeAmount
Release, 9 pages or fewer$10.00
Other instrument, 9 pages or fewer, or principal residence only$20.00
Other instrument, 10 pages or more$75.00
Surcharge, most recordable instruments$40.00
State transfer tax (Cecil and Harford)0.50% of consideration
State transfer tax, first-time Maryland buyer, principal residence0.25%

Harford treats recording fees as non-refundable, and a state transfer tax refund requires a claim form filed with the clerk. There, copies run $0.50 a page and certification is $5.00. Count the deed's pages, since that decides the tier.

sections.h2: Recordation and transfer taxes by county
sections.html:
Only the state transfer tax is uniform. Recordation tax and county transfer tax vary by county, so get the local figure from your title company or the county revenue office.

Baltimore County adds 1.5 percent of consideration as county transfer tax, plus recordation tax at $2.50 per $500 or part of $500. Cecil County's clerk lists recordation tax at $4.10 per $500, rounded, of the actual consideration. Harford splits collection: the county's Revenue Collections office on South Main Street in Bel Air takes county transfer and recordation taxes, while the clerk takes recording fees and state transfer tax.

Depending on the county, checks go to the Clerk of the Circuit Court, to the county government, or to both. When transfer tax comes out of your proceeds, request an itemized estimate before signing.

  • Baltimore County: make payment to Baltimore County, Maryland, through the Office of Budget and Finance in Towson.
  • Harford County: county taxes go to Harford County Revenue, fees to the Clerk.
  • Cecil County: pay fees at the Department of Finance.

sections.h2: Exemptions that lower the tax bill
sections.html:
State law allows counties to exempt part of the tax for first-time buyers of owner-occupied homes, and some family and estate transfers owe nothing at all. Claim any exemption on the intake sheet. Harford requires the full exemption code, or the full tax is charged.

Under Tax-Property Article 12-103(b), a county or Baltimore City may adopt a recordation tax exemption on a set amount of consideration for owner-occupied residential property, if the buyer will occupy the home for at least 7 months of a 12-month period. A second option covers a person who has never owned a Maryland principal residence and will occupy the property, and each grantee signs a sworn statement. The state transfer tax has a first-time buyer rate of 0.25 percent, with the same sworn statement from each grantee.

Deeds under the state's new transfer-on-death law also escape state recordation tax, state transfer tax and county transfer tax if the property is the owner's primary or secondary residence (Chapter 751 of the 2026 laws). Inheritance tax can still apply to heirs.

sections.h2: Problems sellers and heirs run into
sections.html:
Four problems come up again and again: a missing lien certificate, unpaid taxes, a wrong legal description, and an earlier deed that was never recorded. Any of them can halt the clerk or the title company.

Estate sales add steps, because the intake sheet must name the parties and the instrument type correctly, and the preparer certification still applies to the deed.

Even without a deed, moving ownership of a company that holds real estate can be taxed as though a deed were recorded. Moving more than 80 percent of the equity in an entity that owns real property can trigger recordation tax under Tax-Property 12-117, with transfer tax extended by 13-103. If you hold a rental house in an LLC, check this before selling membership interests.

Sellers who live out of state face one more item: Comptroller withholding on nonresident real property sales may apply, and the Clerk collects it.

  • Check that the legal description matches the last recorded deed.
  • Clear any county water, sewer or tax charges before the lien certificate is ordered.
  • Find out early whether an exemption applies and collect the sworn statements.
  • For an inherited house, settle who has authority to sign before anyone drafts the deed.

A cash sale follows the same recording path with fewer pieces. Without a lender, no new deed of trust needs recording next to the deed, and the file normally closes after the title company confirms the lien certificate and taxes.

A deed is still signed, and the clerk still gets the intake sheet and fees. Cash Home Buyers can buy houses in Maryland as-is, including homes with open liens or title questions that need to be cleared at closing. The transfer isn't complete until the deed is recorded, so ask the title company for the recording date and for who pays each tax line.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Maryland?
faqs.a: With the Clerk of the Circuit Court in the county where the property is located. Many counties accept e-recording, mail and walk-in filing, and some route deeds through a county revenue office first.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Maryland?
faqs.a: The clerk's fee is $20 for most deeds of nine pages or fewer and $75 for ten pages or more, plus a $40 surcharge. Transfer and recordation taxes are charged separately and vary by county.

faqs.q: What is the Maryland state transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The state rate in Cecil and Harford is 0.50 percent of the consideration, or 0.25 percent for a first-time Maryland buyer who will use the home as a principal residence. Sworn statements are required for the lower rate.

faqs.q: Can a deed be recorded without a lien certificate?
faqs.a: Generally no. Real Property Article 3-104 requires the collector's certificate for a change-of-ownership instrument, and Baltimore County won't process a deed without one.

faqs.q: Does a transfer-on-death deed need to be recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Chapter 751 of the 2026 laws, a transfer-on-death deed is effective only if it is recorded in the county land records before the owner dies.
